303	The server values come from `duration_ms` in the replicas' request log records, taken from
304	`docker compose logs app` and filtered by the run's payer. `duration_ms` runs from the request
305	entering the middleware to the response, lock waits included.
306	
307	**Planned run.** All 40 requests come from one payer, so they run one after another on its row
308	lock. Each duration includes waiting behind up to three other maximal batches.
309	
310	- The median, 196.0 ms, is within the budget.
311	- The maximum is over it: 257.6 ms at the client and 256.4 ms at the server, about 7 ms above
312	  250 ms.
313	
314	**Supplementary run.** Without contention, a 1,000-payment request takes 50.3 ms median and
315	69.9 ms at most, end to end. Locks are held only inside the transaction, which is part of the
316	request. So these are upper bounds on how long a maximal batch holds its locks: about a quarter
317	of the 250 ms budget.
318	
319	For comparison, the spec 5.7 probe measured 109 ms of lock hold and 126 ms for the whole
320	transaction at 1,000 payments.
321	
322	**Decision.** The batch limit stays at 1,000. The overrun in the planned run is queueing behind
323	other batches of the same payer.
324	
325	## Stand checks
326	
327	These checks were run on Podman 5.8.2 with Docker Compose v5.1.3. They were first done in
328	Task 1 and repeated here.
329	
330	**S1.** Run after `make up`. `docker compose up -d --wait` exited 0, and every container was
331	reported `Healthy`. `docker compose ps -a` showed:
332	
333	```
334	NAME                                   IMAGE                                    COMMAND                  SERVICE   CREATED          STATUS                    PORTS
335	ta-firm-payments-challenge-app-1       docker.io/library/firm-payments:latest   "uvicorn app.main:ap…"   app       13 seconds ago   Up 11 seconds
336	ta-firm-payments-challenge-app-2       docker.io/library/firm-payments:latest   "uvicorn app.main:ap…"   app       13 seconds ago   Up 10 seconds
337	ta-firm-payments-challenge-app-3       docker.io/library/firm-payments:latest   "uvicorn app.main:ap…"   app       13 seconds ago   Up 11 seconds
338	ta-firm-payments-challenge-db-1        docker.io/library/postgres:18            "postgres"               db        2 hours ago      Up 2 hours                127.0.0.1:5432->5432/tcp
339	ta-firm-payments-challenge-lb-1        docker.io/library/nginx:stable           "nginx -g daemon off;"   lb        2 hours ago      Up 7 seconds              0.0.0.0:8000->80/tcp
340	ta-firm-payments-challenge-migrate-1   docker.io/library/firm-payments:latest   "alembic upgrade head"   migrate   13 seconds ago   Exited (0) 1 second ago
341	```
342	
343	Under Podman, `ps` does not print `(healthy)`. `docker inspect -f '{{.State.Health.Status}}'`
344	gave `healthy` for all three app containers. `up -d --wait` starts the one-shot `migrate`
345	service again each time; `alembic upgrade head` then has nothing to do.
346	
347	**S2.** 30 requests to `GET http://localhost:8000/healthz` gave these `X-Upstream` counts:
348	
349	| Replica | Requests |
350	|---|---|
351	| 10.89.2.87:8000 | 8 |
352	| 10.89.2.88:8000 | 13 |
353	| 10.89.2.89:8000 | 9 |
354	
355	That is three distinct values. The distribution right after a balancer restart is not strict
356	round-robin.
357	
358	**S3.** The check started on a freshly seeded database (`make reset`).
359	`docker stop $(docker compose ps -q app | head -1)` stopped `app-1` (10.89.2.88). Then
360	`sample-request.json` was posted five times with `Idempotency-Key: s3`:
361	
362	| Request | Status | `Idempotent-Replayed` | `X-Upstream` | Time, s |
363	|---|---|---|---|---|
364	| 1 | 201 | absent | `10.89.2.88:8000, 10.89.2.89:8000` | 2.030 |
365	| 2 | 201 | true | `10.89.2.87:8000` | 0.007 |
366	| 3 | 201 | true | `10.89.2.89:8000` | 0.006 |
367	| 4 | 201 | true | `10.89.2.87:8000` | 0.005 |
368	| 5 | 201 | true | `10.89.2.89:8000` | 0.005 |
369	
370	Request 1 took 2 s because nginx first tried the stopped replica. Its address no longer
371	answered, so the connect timed out after `proxy_connect_timeout` (2 s) instead of being refused.
372	nginx then passed the request to the next replica. Nothing had been sent to the stopped replica,
373	so passing the POST on was safe.
374	
375	Afterwards:
376	
377	- The five bodies were byte-identical.
378	- The balances changed once: Pinecrest 3,674,875, Lopez 170,075 and Nair 1,405,050.
379	- The database held 3 payment rows and 1 key row.
380	
381	**Restore.** `make up` started the replicas again and restarted `lb`. The image had been rebuilt
382	by `make load --build`, so all three replicas were recreated with new addresses. S2 was then
383	run again with 30 requests:
384	
385	| Replica | Requests |
386	|---|---|
387	| 10.89.2.103:8000 | 8 |
388	| 10.89.2.104:8000 | 13 |
389	| 10.89.2.105:8000 | 9 |
390	
391	Again three distinct values. `make reset` then returned the database to the three seeded firms.
392	
393	**Podman.** Nothing in the stand needed a Podman workaround:
394	
395	- three replicas started;
396	- the service name resolved to every replica, since there were three `X-Upstream` values;
397	- `--wait` waited for health.
398	
399	The only visible difference is the missing `(healthy)` in `ps`.

amounts = [random_amount(rng) for _ in payees]
        bodies.append(batch(payer, payees, amounts, label))

def send_all(base_url: str, bodies: list[bytes], concurrency: int) -> tuple[list[Outcome], float]:
    """Post every body with `concurrency` threads; return the outcomes and the wall time."""
    clients: queue.SimpleQueue[httpx2.Client] = queue.SimpleQueue()
    for _ in range(concurrency):
        clients.put(httpx2.Client(base_url=base_url, timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S, trust_env=False))
    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}

    def send(body: bytes) -> Outcome:
        client = clients.get()
        started = time.perf_counter()
        try:
            response = client.post("/bulk-payments", content=body, headers=headers)
            elapsed_ms = (time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000
        except httpx2.HTTPError as exc:
            elapsed_ms = (time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000
            return Outcome(None, type(exc).__name__, None, elapsed_ms)
        finally:
            clients.put(client)
        error = None
        if response.status_code != 201:
            try:
                error = str(response.json()["error"]["code"])
            except ValueError, KeyError, TypeError:
                error = "unparsed body"
        return Outcome(response.status_code, error, response.headers.get("X-Upstream"), elapsed_ms)

    started = time.perf_counter()
    try:
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=concurrency) as executor:
            outcomes = list(executor.map(send, bodies))
    finally:
        wall_s = time.perf_counter() - started
        for _ in range(concurrency):
            clients.get().close()
    return outcomes, wall_s


def percentile(sorted_values: list[float], p: float) -> float:
    """Nearest-rank percentile."""
    rank = max(1, math.ceil(p / 100 * len(sorted_values)))
    return sorted_values[rank - 1]


def counts(counter: Counter[Any]) -> str:
    return "  ".join(f"{key}: {n}" for key, n in sorted(counter.items(), key=str)) or "-"


def report(args: argparse.Namespace, outcomes: list[Outcome], wall_s: float) -> None:
    durations = sorted(outcome.duration_ms for outcome in outcomes)
    print(f"scenario      {args.scenario}")
    print(f"requests      {len(outcomes)} (concurrency {args.concurrency})")
    print(f"wall time     {wall_s:.3f} s")
    print(f"requests/s    {len(outcomes) / wall_s:.1f}")
    print(
        "latency ms    "
        + "  ".join(f"p{p} {percentile(durations, p):.1f}" for p in (50, 95, 99))
        + f"  max {durations[-1]:.1f}"
    )
    print(f"statuses      {counts(Counter(str(o.status or 'no response') for o in outcomes))}")
    print(f"errors        {counts(Counter(o.error for o in outcomes if o.error))}")
    print(f"upstreams     {counts(Counter(o.upstream for o in outcomes if o.upstream))}")
    if args.scenario == "max-batch":
        median = statistics.median(durations)
        print(
            f"max-batch     {MAX_BATCH_SIZE} payments per request: median {median:.1f} ms,"
            f" max {durations[-1]:.1f} ms; budget {MAX_BATCH_BUDGET_MS} ms (spec 5.7)"
        )
        if args.concurrency > 1:
            print(
                "              all requests share one payer, so these durations include"
                " waiting for its row lock"
            )


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])

**Final state.**
- `make reset`: 3 firms (1: 5000000, 2: 50000, 3: 200000), 0 payments, 0 keys.
- After `make check`, the stand is still up: 3 healthy replicas behind `lb`. One more S2 gave 10 / 11 / 9 over three upstreams.

## Files changed

- Commit 2639070: `app/db.py`, `app/main.py`, `tests/unit/test_get_engine.py` (new).
- Commit 3a603ed: `tests/concurrency/test_multiprocess.py` (new), `scripts/load.py` (new), `Makefile`, `docs/verification-notes.md`.
- Nothing under `.superpowers/` or `docs/assignment.md` was committed. `git status` is clean apart from this report, which is ignored.

## Self-review and concerns

1. **max-batch is over budget in the planned run:** a maximum of 257.6 ms against 250 ms, caused by queueing behind the same payer. The uncontended maximum is 69.9 ms. The limit is unchanged; this is reported, not fixed.
2. **I changed `load.py` after the recorded runs.** I moved the end-of-request timestamp before returning the client to the queue; it was after one `SimpleQueue.put` call before. This is a sub-microsecond difference in the timed region. A 100-request `hot-payee` smoke run after the edit passed, and `make reset` followed it. I did not repeat the recorded runs.
3. **The script's checks go beyond the brief:** the ledger check, the payment rows against the 201 responses, and "every request answered" (a transport error fails the run). 503 is counted and is not a failure. The docstring and the notes state this.
4. **`load.py` reserves firm ids from 1000 in the target database.** Its cleanup also deletes payments between those firms and any other firm.
5. **S3, observed under Podman:** a stopped replica's address times out instead of refusing the connection. nginx therefore spends `proxy_connect_timeout` (2 s) before passing the request on. With the default `fail_timeout` of 10 s, this probably repeats about every 10 s while a replica is down (inferred, not measured). This may be worth a README line.
6. **`make load` rebuilds the image** (`run --build`, like `make test` and `make lint`). The next `make up` therefore recreates the replicas, which get new addresses; `make up` restarts `lb`, so routing stays correct.
7. **The test fixture uses a private attribute:** `test_get_engine.py` resets the engine through `app.db._engine`.
8. **The README still needs the measurements** (spec 13.5); that is Task 9. The figures come from a laptop VM where the client shares the 6 CPUs with the stand.

from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Request, Response
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from sqlalchemy import text
from sqlalchemy.exc import SQLAlchemyError
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.config import Settings, get_settings
from app.db import get_session
from app.schemas import BulkPaymentRequest
from app.service import build_command, execute_bulk_payment

BULK_PAYMENTS_PATH = "/bulk-payments"

router = APIRouter()


@router.get("/healthz")
def healthz(
    response: Response, session: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)]
) -> dict[str, str]:
    try:
        session.execute(text("SELECT 1"))
    except SQLAlchemyError:
        response.status_code = 503
        return {"status": "unavailable"}
    return {"status": "ok"}


@router.post(BULK_PAYMENTS_PATH, status_code=201)
def create_bulk_payment(
    payload: BulkPaymentRequest,
    request: Request,
    session: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)],
    settings: Annotated[Settings, Depends(get_settings)],
) -> JSONResponse:
    # Fields for the per-request log record written in app.main.
    request.state.payer = str(payload.payer_firm_uuid)
    request.state.payment_count = len(payload.payments)
    # Spec 8.1: if the header is sent more than once, the first value is used.
    keys = request.headers.getlist("Idempotency-Key")
    command = build_command(payload, keys[0] if keys else None, settings)
    request.state.total_cents = command.total_cents

    result = execute_bulk_payment(session, command, settings.lock_timeout_ms)
    request.state.outcome = "replayed" if result.replayed else "created"
    # The original and the replay are serialized the same way, so the bytes match.
    headers = {"Idempotent-Replayed": "true"} if result.replayed else None
    return JSONResponse(result.body, status_code=201, headers=headers)

import json
import logging
import socket
import time
import uuid
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Awaitable, Callable, Mapping
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Any

import anyio.to_thread
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request, Response
from fastapi.exceptions import RequestValidationError
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from starlette.exceptions import HTTPException as StarletteHTTPException

from app.api import BULK_PAYMENTS_PATH, router
from app.config import get_settings
from app.db import get_engine
from app.errors import DomainError, ServiceBusy, ValidationFailed
from app.schemas import format_cents

INSTANCE = socket.gethostname()

request_logger = logging.getLogger("app.requests")

_HTTP_ERROR_CODES = {404: "not_found", 405: "method_not_allowed"}

# Pydantic messages that quote part of the input ("found `z` at 0"), by error type.
_FIXED_MESSAGES = {"uuid_parsing": "Input should be a valid UUID"}


def _configure_logging() -> None:
    # Uvicorn configures only its own loggers; without a handler INFO records are dropped.
    app_logger = logging.getLogger("app")
    if not app_logger.handlers:
        handler = logging.StreamHandler()
        handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter("%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s %(message)s"))
        app_logger.addHandler(handler)
        app_logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    _configure_logging()
    # Synchronous endpoints wait for a thread instead of failing on pool checkout.
    # The limiter can be changed only from the event loop.
    anyio.to_thread.current_default_thread_limiter().total_tokens = get_settings().db_pool_size
    # Built before the first request, so requests never race to create it.
    get_engine()
    yield


async def log_request(
    request: Request, call_next: Callable[[Request], Awaitable[Response]]
) -> Response:
    """Write one record per bulk payment request; descriptions are never logged."""
    if request.url.path != BULK_PAYMENTS_PATH:
        return await call_next(request)
    started = time.perf_counter()
    request_id = request.headers.get("x-request-id") or uuid.uuid4().hex
    status = 500
    try:
        response = await call_next(request)
        status = response.status_code
        return response
    finally:
        state = request.state
        total_cents = getattr(state, "total_cents", None)
        record = {
            "request_id": request_id,
            "instance": INSTANCE,
            "payer": getattr(state, "payer", None),
            "payments": getattr(state, "payment_count", None),
            "total": None if total_cents is None else format_cents(total_cents),
            # Unset only when an exception escaped to the 500 handler.
            "outcome": getattr(state, "outcome", "internal_error"),
            "status": status,
            "duration_ms": round((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000, 1),
        }
        request_logger.info(json.dumps(record))


def _error_response(
    request: Request,
    status_code: int,
    code: str,
    message: str,
    *,
    details: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
) -> JSONResponse:
    request.state.outcome = code
    error: dict[str, Any] = {"code": code, "message": message}
    if details is not None:
        error["details"] = details
    return JSONResponse({"error": error}, status_code=status_code, headers=headers)


async def handle_domain_error(request: Request, exc: DomainError) -> JSONResponse:
    details = exc.details if isinstance(exc, ValidationFailed) else None
    headers = {"Retry-After": "1"} if isinstance(exc, ServiceBusy) else None
    return _error_response(
        request, exc.status_code, exc.code, exc.message, details=details, headers=headers
    )


async def handle_request_validation_error(
    request: Request, exc: RequestValidationError
) -> JSONResponse:
    # Only loc, msg and type: input and ctx carry the rejected value, which may be
    # sensitive or impossible to encode (a lone surrogate from a \ud800 escape).
    details = [
        {
            "loc": list(error["loc"]),
            "msg": _FIXED_MESSAGES.get(error["type"], error["msg"]),
            "type": error["type"],
        }
        for error in exc.errors()
    ]
    return _error_response(
        request, 422, "validation_error", "the request is invalid", details=details
    )


async def handle_http_exception(request: Request, exc: StarletteHTTPException) -> JSONResponse:
    if exc.status_code == 400:
        # FastAPI raises 400 only when it cannot read the body as JSON, for
        # example invalid UTF-8; spec section 8.1 makes that a validation error.
        message = "the request body is not valid JSON"
        detail = {"loc": ["body"], "msg": message, "type": "json_invalid"}
        return _error_response(request, 422, "validation_error", message, details=[detail])
    code = _HTTP_ERROR_CODES.get(exc.status_code, "http_error")
    return _error_response(request, exc.status_code, code, str(exc.detail), headers=exc.headers)


async def handle_internal_error(request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:
    # Uvicorn logs the traceback; the client learns nothing about the cause.
    return _error_response(request, 500, "internal_error", "internal server error")


def create_app() -> FastAPI:
    application = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
    application.include_router(router)
    application.middleware("http")(log_request)
    application.exception_handler(DomainError)(handle_domain_error)
    application.exception_handler(RequestValidationError)(handle_request_validation_error)
    application.exception_handler(StarletteHTTPException)(handle_http_exception)
    application.exception_handler(Exception)(handle_internal_error)
    return application


app = create_app()

    request_id = request.headers.get("x-request-id") or uuid.uuid4().hex
    status = 500
    try:
        response = await call_next(request)
        status = response.status_code
        return response
    finally:
        state = request.state
        total_cents = getattr(state, "total_cents", None)
        record = {
            "request_id": request_id,
            "instance": INSTANCE,
            "payer": getattr(state, "payer", None),
            "payments": getattr(state, "payment_count", None),
            "total": None if total_cents is None else format_cents(total_cents),
            # Unset only when an exception escaped to the 500 handler.
            "outcome": getattr(state, "outcome", "internal_error"),
            "status": status,
            "duration_ms": round((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000, 1),
        }
        request_logger.info(json.dumps(record))


def _error_response(
    request: Request,
    status_code: int,
    code: str,
    message: str,
    *,
    details: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
) -> JSONResponse:
    request.state.outcome = code
    error: dict[str, Any] = {"code": code, "message": message}
    if details is not None:
        error["details"] = details
    return JSONResponse({"error": error}, status_code=status_code, headers=headers)


async def handle_domain_error(request: Request, exc: DomainError) -> JSONResponse:
    details = exc.details if isinstance(exc, ValidationFailed) else None
    headers = {"Retry-After": "1"} if isinstance(exc, ServiceBusy) else None
    return _error_response(
        request, exc.status_code, exc.code, exc.message, details=details, headers=headers
    )


def _is_json_content_type(content_type: str | None) -> bool:
    """FastAPI's rule: only application/json and application/*+json bodies are parsed.

    Without the header the body is not parsed either (strict_content_type).
    """
    if not content_type:
        return False
    message = email.message.Message()
    message["content-type"] = content_type
    subtype = message.get_content_subtype()
    return message.get_content_maintype() == "application" and (
        subtype == "json" or subtype.endswith("+json")
    )


async def handle_request_validation_error(
    request: Request, exc: RequestValidationError
) -> JSONResponse:
    # Only loc, msg and type: input and ctx carry the rejected value, which may be
    # sensitive or impossible to encode (a lone surrogate from a \ud800 escape).
    details = [
        {
            "loc": list(error["loc"]),
            "msg": _FIXED_MESSAGES.get(error["type"], error["msg"]),
            "type": error["type"],
        }
        for error in exc.errors()
    ]
    if _is_json_content_type(request.headers.get("content-type")):
        message = "the request is invalid"
    else:
        # The body reached validation as raw bytes, for example from `curl -d`.
        message = "the request body must be JSON sent with Content-Type: application/json"
    return _error_response(request, 422, "validation_error", message, details=details)


async def handle_http_exception(request: Request, exc: StarletteHTTPException) -> JSONResponse:
    if exc.status_code == 400:
        # FastAPI raises 400 only when it cannot read the body as JSON, for
        # example invalid UTF-8; spec section 8.1 makes that a validation error.
        message = "the request body is not valid JSON"
        detail = {"loc": ["body"], "msg": message, "type": "json_invalid"}
        return _error_response(request, 422, "validation_error", message, details=[detail])
    code = _HTTP_ERROR_CODES.get(exc.status_code, "http_error")
    return _error_response(request, exc.status_code, code, str(exc.detail), headers=exc.headers)


async def handle_internal_error(request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:
    # Uvicorn logs the traceback; the client learns nothing about the cause.
    return _error_response(request, 500, "internal_error", "internal server error")


def create_app() -> FastAPI:
    application = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
    application.include_router(router)
    application.middleware("http")(log_request)
    application.exception_handler(DomainError)(handle_domain_error)
    application.exception_handler(RequestValidationError)(handle_request_validation_error)
    application.exception_handler(StarletteHTTPException)(handle_http_exception)
    application.exception_handler(Exception)(handle_internal_error)
    return application


app = create_app()

name: ci

on:
  push:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: docker compose up -d --wait db
      - run: make check

  # The run stand on Docker Engine (spec 13.8): three replicas behind the balancer.
  stand:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    env:
      BASE_URL: http://localhost:8000
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: docker compose version
      - run: make up
      - name: Wait for the balancer
        run: curl -fsS --retry 10 --retry-connrefused --retry-delay 1 "$BASE_URL/healthz"
      - run: make seed
      - name: The sample request returns 201
        run: |
          status=$(curl -sS -o response.json -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
            -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @sample-request.json \
            "$BASE_URL/bulk-payments")
          cat response.json
          echo
          test "$status" = 201
      - name: 30 health checks reach three replicas (S2)
        run: |
          upstreams=$(for _ in $(seq 30); do
            curl -sS -o /dev/null -D - "$BASE_URL/healthz" | tr -d '\r' | grep -i '^x-upstream:'
          done | sort | uniq -c)
          echo "$upstreams"
          test "$(echo "$upstreams" | wc -l)" -eq 3
      - name: Pinecrest balance is 3674875
        run: |
          balance=$(docker compose exec -T db psql -U postgres -d firm_payments -tAc \
            "SELECT balance_cents FROM firms WHERE uuid = '3f1c9a2e-7b4d-4c1e-9a55-2d8e6f0b7c41'")
          echo "balance_cents=$balance"
          test "$balance" = 3674875
      - name: Stand state
        if: failure()
        run: |
          docker compose ps -a
          docker compose logs --no-color

import yaml
wf = yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/ci.yml'))
jobs = wf['jobs']
print('top-level keys:', list(wf))
print('jobs:', list(jobs))
for name, job in jobs.items():
    print(name, 'runs-on', job['runs-on'], 'steps', len(job['steps']))
    for step in job['steps']:
        assert ('uses' in step) != ('run' in step), step
        print('   ', step.get('name') or step.get('uses') or step['run'].splitlines()[0], '| if:', step.get('if'))
" && cat > $S/ci_dryrun.py <<'EOF'
"""Run the `stand` job's run: blocks from ci.yml locally, as GitHub would.

GitHub runs each `run:` with `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail {0}` when
`shell: bash`; steps stop at the first failure, then `if: failure()` steps run.
Usage: ci_dryrun.py <ci.yml> <job> [extra KEY=VALUE env ...] [--only NAME-SUBSTRING]
"""
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

import yaml

path, job_name, *rest = sys.argv[1:]
only = None
if "--only" in rest:
    i = rest.index("--only")
    only = rest[i + 1]
    rest = rest[:i] + rest[i + 2 :]
job = yaml.safe_load(open(path))["jobs"][job_name]
assert job["defaults"]["run"]["shell"] == "bash"
env = {**os.environ, **{k: str(v) for k, v in job.get("env", {}).items()}}
env.update(kv.split("=", 1) for kv in rest)
failed = False
for step in job["steps"]:
    if "uses" in step:
        print(f"--- skip uses: {step['uses']} (the working tree is the checkout)")
        continue
    name = step.get("name") or step["run"].splitlines()[0]
    if only and only not in name and step.get("if") != "failure()":
        continue
    cond = step.get("if")
    if cond == "failure()" and not failed:
        print(f"--- skip (no failure): {name}")
        continue
    if failed and cond != "failure()":
        print(f"--- skip (earlier step failed): {name}")
        continue
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".sh", delete=False) as f:
        f.write(step["run"])
    print(f"=== step: {name}", flush=True)
    rc = subprocess.call(["bash", "--noprofile", "--norc", "-eo", "pipefail", f.name], env=env)
    print(f"=== exit {rc}: {name}", flush=True)
    if rc != 0:
        failed = True
sys.exit(1 if failed else 0)
EOF

# Final fix wave: report

Implementer: Claude Opus 5.5. Branch `feat/bulk-payment-service`, FIX_BASE 3a603ed. No push, no branch switch, no history rewrite. Nothing under `.superpowers/` was committed; this report is git-ignored (`.gitignore:17`).

Status: DONE_WITH_CONCERNS. All six findings are fixed and verified. The concerns are listed at the end; none of them blocks.

## Commits

| SHA | Subject | Findings |
|---|---|---|
| bf1a9e5 | fix: name application/json when the body is not sent as JSON | 1 |
| c9d7093 | fix: raise the balancer's body limit and pass the client's Host | 4, 5 |
| ca03d4a | fix: configurable host ports, balancer on loopback | 3 |
| 92d8770 | ci: run the stand on Docker Engine | 2 |
| 65a3760 | docs: qualify the C3 plan count, the load.py edit and the medians | 6 |

Every commit ends with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`; checked with `git log --format='%(trailers:key=Co-Authored-By,valueonly)'`.

## Finding 1: Content-Type message

**Change (app/main.py).** I added `_is_json_content_type()`, which copies FastAPI 0.165's own rule from `fastapi/routing.py` lines 474–484:

- A body is parsed as JSON only for `application/json` or `application/*+json`. Parameters and case are ignored, through `email.message.Message`.
- A missing header counts as not JSON. Since `strict_content_type` defaults to True, FastAPI does not parse such a body.

`handle_request_validation_error` keeps the 422, the `validation_error` code and the `details` list (loc/msg/type only). Only the message changes:

- When the Content-Type is not JSON, the message is "the request body must be JSON sent with Content-Type: application/json".
- Otherwise it is still "the request is invalid".

The 400 → 422 path for invalid UTF-8 is unchanged; it always has a JSON Content-Type.

**Tests (tests/api/test_validation.py).**

- `test_non_json_content_type_names_application_json` posts the bytes of `sample-request.json` three ways: `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (what `curl -d` sends), `text/plain`, and with no Content-Type at all. httpx2 adds none for `content=`; I checked the request headers. Each case asserts:
  - 422 with `validation_error`;
  - detail keys exactly {loc, msg, type}, through `assert_validation_error`;
  - `"Content-Type: application/json"` in the message;
  - none of the sample's descriptions in the response text (Ruling 12);
  - no payment rows.
- `test_json_content_type_keeps_generic_message` is a guard on the condition. It covers `application/json`, `Application/JSON; charset=utf-8` and `application/vnd.api+json`, each with body `[]`, and expects the message "the request is invalid".

**RED**, with the new tests in place and `app/main.py` unchanged:

```
$ uv run pytest -q tests/api/test_validation.py -k content_type
E       AssertionError: assert 'Content-Type: application/json' in 'the request is invalid'
FAILED tests/api/test_validation.py::test_non_json_content_type_names_application_json[form_urlencoded]
FAILED tests/api/test_validation.py::test_non_json_content_type_names_application_json[text_plain]
FAILED tests/api/test_validation.py::test_non_json_content_type_names_application_json[missing]
3 failed, 3 passed, 25 deselected in 0.13s
```

The three guard cases pass before and after the fix, as intended.

**GREEN:**

```
$ uv run pytest -q tests/api/test_validation.py
31 passed in 0.28s
$ uv run pytest -q
151 passed in 6.02s
```

The 151 are the previous 145 plus the 6 new cases. ruff and mypy are clean.

**On the stand** (port 8000, replicas rebuilt with this commit). Before:

```
$ curl -X POST localhost:8000/bulk-payments -d @sample-request.json
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","message":"the request is invalid","details":[{"loc":["body"],"msg":"Input should be a valid dictionary or object to extract fields from","type":"model_attributes_type"}]}}
HTTP 422
```

After:

```
$ curl -X POST localhost:8000/bulk-payments -d @sample-request.json
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","message":"the request body must be JSON sent with Content-Type: application/json","details":[{"loc":["body"],"msg":"Input should be a valid dictionary or object to extract fields from","type":"model_attributes_type"}]}}
HTTP 422
$ curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' --data-binary @sample-request.json localhost:8000/bulk-payments
(same body) HTTP 422

- Percentiles are nearest-rank.

**A change to `scripts/load.py` after the runs.** After the runs above, one timing line in
`send()` was moved: the end-of-request timestamp is now taken before the HTTP client is returned
to the pool, and was taken after it before. The old timed region therefore also contained one
`SimpleQueue.put` on an unbounded queue, which never blocks; `timeit` puts the call at about
10 ns on the host. It could lengthen a client duration by that much, which is far below the
0.1 ms the figures are given to, so it cannot change any recorded figure. Wall time and
requests/s are timed outside `send()`, and the statuses, `X-Upstream` counts, ledger checks and
server `duration_ms` values do not pass through that line. The runs were not repeated after the
edit.

input.message:
Status: DONE_WITH_CONCERNS. All six findings are fixed and checked on the stand. The stand is at the seed (3 firms, 0 payments, 0 keys) with three replicas behind the balancer, and the tree is clean.

Commits:
- bf1a9e5 fix: name application/json when the body is not sent as JSON
- c9d7093 fix: raise the balancer's body limit and pass the client's Host
- ca03d4a fix: configurable host ports, balancer on loopback
- 92d8770 ci: run the stand on Docker Engine
- 65a3760 docs: qualify the C3 plan count, the load.py edit and the medians
- 2f4d609 docs: state why wall time is unaffected by the load.py edit

Tests: 151 passed on the host and in `make check`; ruff and mypy are clean. Finding 1 went RED (3 failed) then GREEN.

Findings:
1. Done. With the default curl form encoding, `curl -d @sample-request.json` on the stand now gets a 422 whose message names `Content-Type: application/json`. A request with no Content-Type gets the same message, because FastAPI does not parse it.
2. Done, but never run on GitHub. The YAML parses. I ran the new `stand` job's own commands on a fresh separate Compose project (Podman, Compose v5.1.3) and they passed. A deliberately wrong balance failed the check and printed `ps -a` and the logs.
3. Done; host-side tests follow `DB_PORT`. With `LB_PORT=8001 DB_PORT=5433 make up`, 8001 answered and 8000 refused. `DB_PORT=5433 uv run pytest` passed 151 and fails without the variable. `make up` restored the defaults with the data intact.
4. Done. A 1,098,073-byte batch (1,000 payments, 500-character non-ASCII descriptions) now returns 201 instead of nginx's HTML 413.
5. Done. `POST /bulk-payments/` now redirects to `http://localhost:8000/bulk-payments`, keeping the port.
6. Done. Spec and plan do not quote the old 422 message.

Concerns: the CI stand job is unproven on Docker Engine until the first push. README items: bodies over 8 MB still get an HTML 413; `scripts/load.py` host defaults ignore `DB_PORT`/`LB_PORT`; the S1 output in the notes still shows the old `0.0.0.0:8000` binding.

Report: /Users/<user>/Development/taxdome/ta-firm-payments-challenge/.superpowers/sdd/plan/final-fix-report.md
